kept.excerpt: The full effects of increases in the cash rate from earlier in the year will take time to materialise. This does mean that some further easing in the growth of demand is likely to be required if we’re to bring inflation back down sustainably to target. A key question in the period ahead is whether the tightening in monetary policy earlier in the year is sufficient to achieve this. The Board is prepared to act as required to achieve its mandate, including by increasing the cash rate further if needed.
kept.relevance: Governor Bullock’s cutoff-day speech identifies the central choice ahead of August: allow earlier tightening more time to work or raise rates further to contain persistent inflation.

kept.excerpt: In a speech in Sydney, Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock said a key uncertainty was whether the three rate hikes already delivered this year were enough to return inflation to its 2%-3% target band. She said the economy was slowing as expected but the housing market has weakened more than forecast, and the central bank was watching how changes in house prices affect household spending and investment decisions.
kept.relevance: Contemporaneous reporting documents both the unresolved inflation problem and evidence of slowing activity relevant to an August hold.

kept.excerpt: In June 2026, employment increased by 76,300 people (0.5%) to 14,823,300 people in seasonally adjusted terms. Full-time employment increased by 29,300 to 10,173,500 people, and part-time employment increased by 47,000 to 4,649,800 people.
kept.relevance: The latest labour-force release available by the cutoff shows strong employment growth, a potential counterweight to the case for keeping rates unchanged.

kept.excerpt: Members agreed that financial conditions were now probably somewhat restrictive. Taking these considerations together, members judged that there was merit in using the space provided by the Board’s earlier decisions to raise the cash rate target to assess how the economy was adjusting and the impact of disruptions to oil supply.
kept.relevance: Minutes published on June 30 explain the Board’s rationale for pausing and provide an official framework for assessing whether that rationale could persist into August.

kept.excerpt: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 4.0 per cent in the 12 months to May 2026, according to the latest data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS). ‘Trimmed mean annual inflation was 3.6 per cent in the 12 months to May 2026, up from 3.4 per cent in the 12 months to April 2026,’ Ms McCririck said.
kept.relevance: The latest inflation release available by the cutoff shows underlying inflation accelerating and remaining above the RBA’s target despite lower headline inflation.

kept.excerpt: At its meeting today, the Board decided to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35 per cent. Following the three increases in the cash rate target since the beginning of the year, financial conditions are now tighter than they were, and there are signs that the economy is slowing as expected. But inflation is still too high and the Board judged that it was appropriate to leave the cash rate target unchanged while it assesses the response to previous interest rate rises and the impact of the oil supply disruption. Today’s policy decision was unanimous.
kept.relevance: The most recent policy decision before the cutoff establishes the 4.35% cash-rate baseline and the unanimous decision to await evidence on earlier tightening.

kept.excerpt: At its meeting today, the Board decided to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.35 per cent. Today’s policy decision was made by majority: eight members voted to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.35 per cent; one member voted to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.10 per cent.
kept.relevance: The preceding rate increase establishes the recent tightening history and shows that the Board had already demonstrated willingness to respond to upside inflation risks.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-28, inclusive. Used web_search to identify sources and agent-reach web read to verify source text after web_fetch failed. Publication dates were checked against dated releases, speech metadata, Reuters dating, and the RBA announcement identifying June minutes publication on 2026-06-30. The Reuters story carries a July 28 Sydney dateline and a July 27 display timestamp; both fall within the cutoff. Excluded later publications, rolling pages without verifiable publication dates, prediction-market and betting pages, and all odds or market-price figures. No August meeting outcome or post-cutoff data is included. The undated rolling meeting calendar was not included as a dated evidence item.
